Exactly as in the proof of
Lemma <REF_0001>
we claim a quasi-inverse is given by the functor sending
<MATH_0001> to
<MATH_0002>
and in order to prove this it suffices to show that
<MATH_0003> is an isomorphism.
This we may check locally, hence we may and do assume <MATH_0004>
is affine. Then we can find a finite surjective morphism
<MATH_0005> such that there exists an open covering
<MATH_0006> such that <MATH_0007> factors through <MATH_0008>.
See
More on Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0002>.
Applying Lemma
<REF_0003>
we see that it suffices to prove
the lemma after replacing <MATH_0009> by <MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011> and <MATH_0012>
by its base change. Thus we may assume <MATH_0013> has sections Zariski locally.
Of course, using that the problem is local on <MATH_0014> we reduce
to the case where we have a section which is
Lemma <REF_0004>.
